decisions.where: Roles: the Developer item, the people who call invoicer's library from their own code; O2 and its key results, which keep the library behavior they rely on as it is.
Roles: the Developer item, who install the command once for the accounting team; O3 and its key results.
Roles: one Developer item covers both calling the library and installing the command, kept as the person's departure.

Objectives and key results: O2, "after updating invoicer, the developers get the results their own code gave before, without editing their code"; O3, "the developers are left with a command they install once and never need to set up again"; printing is named only under O1.

Roles says only who each role is and the part of the job they come for; the Concept alone says where the invoice lines come from and that the rate is set at each print; the names invoice lines and their own code throughout.
Concept: the idea for O2 keeps "The command only calls the library", the person's words, as their departure.

Objectives and key results: the template's ranking paragraph, "KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 come first: keep a change that improves a key result only if none before it gets worse.", and the template's sentence on no targets and Goodhart's law, as the template writes it.
Objectives and key results: KR1.1, "the share of printed invoices that are wrong or needed a developer's help. Lower is better."
Objectives and key results: the ranking line names only KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1, and doesn't rank KR1.2, KR2.2 and KR3.2 among themselves, as the person accepts.

Objectives and key results: printing without a developer under O1 alone (O1, KR1.1); O3 and KR3.1 and KR3.2 count only the developer's one install; Concept: the one rounding of tax under the idea for O2.
Concept: the one way sentence and its three ideas as the person worded them, two for O1 and one for O2; no idea for the install.

more.where: Objectives and key results: KR1.1 counts "printed invoices that are wrong or needed a developer's help" in place of "print tasks", so a developer counts the same thing each time: each printed invoice, and whether it was wrong or needed a developer's help.

settled.point: the verb of the ranking line
settled.decided: "KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 come first", with "and" before the last id and the plural "come".
settled.ground: The N4 decision 0 words it so; three key results are the subject, so the verb is plural (refactor-doc N5, the sentence reads one way to a machine translator), and the template's "comes" fits its one KR<n>.1.
